value.body: A blasting engineer designs the drilling and explosive patterns that break rock, and supervises blasts so the rock breaks as planned without harming people, machines or nearby homes. Mining companies, quarry and tunnelling contractors, and explosives manufacturers (for technical service at customer sites) hire them. A day involves marking and checking drill holes, overseeing charging, firing the blast and measuring the results.

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers join mining companies or contractors in drill-and-blast sections, or explosives manufacturers as technical service engineers, through campus placement or direct hiring. Handling and firing explosives at mines needs the certificates and permissions set under mine and explosives rules.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Coordinating with drilling and loading crews

value.title: At a glance
items: Safety discipline is central; mistakes can be serious.
Common next roles: senior blasting engineer, drill-and-blast manager, technical service lead.
Tunnelling and infrastructure projects also use blasting skills.
